newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN OLOS TO HEAD FOR VOLATILE PERIOD.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN OLOS TO HEAD FOR VOLATILE PERIOD.

text.p: Volatility looks set to increase in the Belgian linear bond market from Monday as U.S. data releases come back to cast a shadow over already nervous European bond markets, dealers said.

With much of Europe closed on Thursday for May Day, some investors could use the approach of what is likely to become a long weekend as an excuse to close positions, perhaps with a bit of profit-taking, they said.
"May is a strange month on the continent with many long weekends," one trader noted.
Belgian OLOs closed lower on Friday as a French election poll released on Thursday sparked another bout of EMU jitters.
The poll placed France's centre right government only narrowly ahead of left-wing parties, who support EMU but oppose fresh austerity measures to meet the Maastricht criteria.

The benchmark 10-year OLO yield rose to 6.04 percent from 5.99 percent, underperforming Bunds, with the spread over equivalent German paper rising to 15 from 13 basis points. "I don't think the (spread) move is exaggerated. It could even go a bit wider if there is more tension surrounding EMU," one trader commented.

Among U.S. data due for release next week there are durable goods and consumer confidence figures on Tuesday, first quarter GDP data on Wednesday and, on Friday, the all important non-farm payrolls figures for April.

Traders said the uncertainty about EMU and worries about U.S. inflation in the run-up to the U.S. Fed's next policy meeting at the end of May was pushing investors to take shelter in the middle of the yield curve, helping Belgium outperform other markets in that area. Interest for the longer end of the curve dried up on Friday.
